description: Agent Events: submit speaker confirmation records with the published lineup: the lineup with the event and each announced speaker with its id, name and the session named for it; the confirmations with the event and each record with its id, the speaker, the session it names, its status (confirmed, tentative, declined or withdrawn) and the day recorded. The signed report gives the lineup and the confirmations, each announced speaker paired with a record for the same person, preferring one for the same session, every announced speaker with no confirmation named, the status of each record and the session on each side, and counts them, and names a discrepant lineup: an announced speaker with no confirmation record, one recorded as declined or withdrawn and one confirmed for another session than the lineup names; then a tentative confirmation, a confirmed speaker the lineup leaves out and another event name, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. A record with no status, a session named on one side only, or a lineup with no speakers leaves the records unverified. Speakers read as people without case or punctuation and in either name order, and sessions read by their words. This reads the people announced to speak at an event against their own confirmations: wever_coordination-roster-check reads the roster of agents taking part in one job with their identities, roles and rights, and wever_hire-availability-check reads a candidate’s availability or start commitment against a hiring brief’s timeline, while the speaker check reads an event’s published lineup against its speaker confirmation records, speaker by speaker. Verdict event_speaker_discrepant, event_speaker_partial, event_speaker_unverified or event_speaker_consistent. POST /api/event-speaker-check. Reads the event records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads consistency between documents only: it never books a venue, registers or invites anyone, sells or refunds a ticket, publishes an announcement, or judges whether an event should happen, was well run, or was worth attending, only whether its records agree with each other and with what was announced, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Events reads an organized event’s records for consistency between documents: an event brief, a published agenda, speaker confirmations, a registration list, a venue arrangement, a ticketing record, a public announcement and a post-event report, each against the requirements, plan, lineup, capacity and eligibility terms, brief, announced terms, schedule or records it should agree with. Beside it, the Standing jobs rail tools such as wever_schedule-create register, list, report on and cancel recurring jobs and keep state, and wever_meeting-brief states one meeting’s decisions and action items from its notes, while this family keeps no state, registers nothing, runs nothing and reads the records in the call against each other and against what was announced. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-events-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-events/.

speaker.description: The speaker the record is for.

label.description: Optional name recorded in the report.

speakers.description: Each speaker the published lineup announces.

session.description: The session the lineup names for the speaker.
